verdict.rationale: Next.js documents several incremental-adoption paths: starting as a static site or SPA and later adding server features, migrating existing Vite or Create React App apps, and using Multi-Zones to run multiple Next.js apps under one domain. None of this shows embedding the framework into only a small part of an existing page, so the low end of the story is unevidenced. Missing for 10: documented embedding of Next.js into part of an existing (non-Next) page, widget-level or island-style adoption, and hands-on corroboration of a gradual scale-up.

support.subject: As a developer, I can incrementally adopt the framework, scaling from a small part of a page up to a full application

citations.quote: Next.js enables starting as a static site or Single-Page Application (SPA), then later optionally upgrading to use features that require a server.
Learn how to build micro-frontends using Next.js Multi-Zones to deploy multiple Next.js apps under a single domain.
Learn how to migrate your existing React application from Vite to Next.js.
